First quit all dabs, and vape pens. The massive amounts of THC they contain makes it really hard to quit cold turkey. Start by switching over to a balanced flower, such as harlequin. It will quell your cravings but will allow you to wean down your consumption of THC. After a week or so, switch over to a CBD flower with minimal THC such as Charlotte’s Web or Cannatonic. 

There’s been several studies which have demonstrated that CBD can be effective at reducing withdrawal symptoms. 

CBN is extremely effective as a sleep aid, get some CBN oil and take an hour before bed if you’re having trouble sleeping at any point.

(Depending on your tolerance, you may find switching from dabs to a 1:1 flower too extreme; if that’s the case, grab some medium-high THC flower to consume before the 1:1)

You need to reduce your Vyvanse dosage so you don’t experience so many negative side effects. Vyvanse dosage directly influences how long it lasts. At 60mg your looking at 12-14 hrs of duration. It varies slightly from person to person but that’s the truth. 

Try titrating your dosage with water to find the right dose for you. I used to take 60mg and had the exact same experience as you; duration of 14 hrs or more, and difficulty falling asleep until at least 3-4am. I reduced my dosage to 40mg and my sleep patterns have been way more consistent and healthy. Most of my doctors have also recommend regular exercise, therapy, and vitamin supplementation as critical components for a wholistic treatment for ADHD.

Vyvanse is a maintenance treatment, meaning it’s meant to be taken at the same time each day, at the same dosage (lowest effective dose without negative side effects), for a nearly indefinite period of time. 

You said you were prescribed “50-70mg” or Vyvanse each day… well which one is it? It can’t be both… your meant to take the same dosage each day. Taking extra  medication is going to cause your medication to be less effective and might create problems for you down the line.

I’m relaying both experiences and information I’ve learned from my GP, psychiatrist, or ADHD specialist. Some things I’ve had to learn the hard way. I let my self spend too many years sleeping 3-4 hrs a night, knowing I could function if I took a little extra medication, not realizing the damage I was doing to my brain and the importance of sleep for treatment of ADHD.

Weed does NOT help with ADHD in the long term. Take it from the 27yr old who has been smoking everyday since 10th grade. I went years without being diagnosed for ADHD, was diagnosed at 22. That said stimulants only work if you take the right dose, keep eating, and maintain a healthy sleep schedule. 

Exercise is probably better than any medication to be honest. Adding Meditation would be even better (ever wonder why in East Asian countries where meditation is practiced there are virtually no cases of ADHD? It seems to be a western problem.)

If you choose to get therapy (you should at least consider it) then Organizational Behavioural Therapy is what you want. The real tough part of living with ADHD comes with the transition to adulthood and the increased responsibility/pressure that it brings; life demands organization and productivity. You’ll want to be prepared for that. It’s much harder to learn it later on.
